headerBody: Brazil: Tourist Scams maps the exact plays that work the Copacabana sand, the Lapa stairwell bars, the GRU and GIG arrivals halls, and the Pelourinho cobblestones. Every entry is documented against Brazilian police reporting — Polícia Militar (190) and Polícia Civil, the DEAT tourist police — plus PROCON consumer-agency rules, r/Brazil and r/solotravel reports, and verified Brazilian news, then drawn as a bright comic strip so you recognize the setup before it reaches the pitch.
quadHead: Four ways Brazil catches tourists off guard.

quad.title: The Lapa BRL 10,000 Caipirinha Trap
quad.tl: A friendly English-speaker walks you up the stairs of an unmarked Lapa bar, two caipirinhas land at the table, and the bill comes to BRL 10,000 with bouncers between you and the door — the “friend” pockets a 30–50% commission and is gone before the card clears.

quad.title: The Paulista Clown Distraction
quad.tl: Three to five men work Avenida Paulista's MASP underpass and the Consolação metro exits with a “cuidado, caiu algo” (careful, something fell) distraction while a partner lifts your wallet from behind — locals call the ring os palhaços, the clowns, and the look-down is the lift.

quad.title: The Ciudad del Este Counterfeit Run
quad.tl: Across the Ponte da Amizade, Paraguay-side “guides” steer tourists to counterfeit-electronics stalls where an “iPhone 16 BRL 2,500” is stolen or fake, while motoboys run phone-snatches on the crossing and armed-robbery risk on Av. San Blas climbs after 5pm.

quad.title: The SSA Coopataxi Kiosk
quad.tl: A “Special Taxi” or Coopataxi kiosk inside SSA arrivals quotes BRL 320 to your Pelourinho pousada while you're jet-lagged and dragging luggage — the real Uber fare is BRL 70–BRL 130, and after 10pm unauthorized cash-only drivers swarm passengers whose app rides have dropped.

body: Brazil: Tourist Scams is part of the tabiji.ai Travel Safety Series. Every scam is documented against Brazilian police reporting — the Polícia Militar (190) and Polícia Civil, the DEAT tourist police — PROCON consumer-protection rules, r/Brazil and r/solotravel reports, and verified Brazilian news. Sourced and re-reported, not recycled from blog lists.

72 specific scams across Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo, Salvador, Foz do Iguaçu, Manaus and 7 more cities — the airport “special taxi” kiosk, the Lapa caipirinha trap, the Copacabana arrastão sweep, the Paulista clown distraction, the couvert artístico pad. The exact scripts, the red flags that give them away, and the Portuguese phrases that shut them down, written phonetically so you can show them on your phone.
Scams evolve, so the book is re-researched every year, and the current edition sits in your Kindle library. Built for the traveler who wants to move through Brazil relaxed, not braced.
